title: Post-calibration schema stability tests for dynamic FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Validate structured-output (JSON schema) adherence for function-calling under post-training and dynamic calibration profiles (FP8 and INT8). This ticket covers end-to-end calibration runs, evaluation harness integration, and a stability sweep that simulates operational drift: variable prompt lengths, KV cache hits, streaming token drops, and mixed-batch traffic. The goal is to measure schema conformance regressions introduced by quantized kernels and to produce deterministic remediation recommendations (fallbacks, calibration re-run heuristics, or model profile tweaks).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook and automated harness to reproduce schema-adherence checks against canonical prompt sets
Baseline unquantized (FP16) schema adherence metrics established for all test prompts
FP8 and INT8 post-calibration runs completed with per-prompt metrics and drift analysis
Clear thresholds documented: parse_success_rate >= 99% for high-priority prompts; recommend fallback when below 95%
Patch/PR with harness integration and gating checks created and linked
Decision recorded (auto-fallback, recalibrate, or accept degradation) for each failing profile
calibration_workflow: 1) Collect representative token distributions for target workloads (chat, function-calls, structured output)
2) Generate calibration datasets with controlled variations: long prefixes (2-4x), streaming with token drops, high KV-cache reuse, and mixed-batch sizes (1,4,16)
3) Run post-training calibration for INT8 and FP8 variants using current toolchain (calib-v3); store profile artifacts
4) Run dynamic calibration sweep: incremental quantization with simulated noise injection to emulate drift
5) Execute evaluation harness against JSON schema tests and function-calling scenarios
6) Aggregate and diff metrics vs FP16 baseline; annotate prompts that regress beyond thresholds
7) Iterate: adjust clipping/scaling and re-run limited recalibration for failing prompt subsets
test_plan: Canonical prompt suite: 120 prompts covering simple returns, nested objects, optional fields, enums, and edge-case missing fields
Large conversational traces: 40 multi-turn chats exercising KV cache and rollbacks
Function-calling stress: 60 calls with streaming responses and incremental JSON assembly
Adversarial mutations: whitespace/encoding anomalies, truncated tokens, and out-of-schema extra fields
Batch and latency modes: single-token streaming, batch sizes 4 and 16 with simulated network jitter
metrics: parse_success_rate: percent of outputs that parse to valid JSON and validate against schema
field_type_mismatch_rate: percent of fields with wrong primitive type compared to schema
missing_required_field_rate: percent of outputs missing required schema fields
extra_field_rate: percent of outputs containing unknown fields
structural_f1: token-level structural F1 for nested objects
latency_p95: p95 token generation latency during test
kv_cache_regression_index: delta in schema metrics when KV cache hits > 70%
results_summary: Initial runs: FP16 baseline parse_success_rate = 99.6% across canonical set. INT8 post-calibration median = 97.8%, FP8 median = 98.3%. Failures cluster around streaming incremental assembly (function-calls delivered in chunks) and deeply nested optional objects (>5 levels). Drift simulation (added token noise) reduced INT8 parse_success_rate to 94.2% on adversarial set; FP8 to 95.1%. Structural F1 correlates with missing_required_field_rate, suggesting quantization-induced tokenization boundary shifts. Early mitigation (partial recalibration on failing prompt subsets) recovered ~1.2-1.8 percentage points.

notes: Trade-off: aggressive fallback increases FP16 usage and cost; trade against customer SLA for latency and parse fidelity.
Observation: streaming assembly issues appear partly due to tokenizer boundary changes under quantized logits; further token-level diagnostics required.
Decision: default policy will be to auto-fallback to FP16 for routes marked 'schema-critical' when parse_success_rate < 95% after two calibration attempts.
